measuredBy: ai:1, corroborated by ai:2 on an independent corpus
what: False-alarm rate of the author-side mangled-Swedish check, measured on real agent-authored history before the check was allowed to block anything.
criterion: A paragraph is flagged when it has at least minParagraphWords word tokens, contains no a-ring/umlaut at all, and contains at least minSwedishMarkers distinct Swedish function words. A single diacritic anywhere clears the paragraph.

theTicketsHypothesisWasWrong.hypothesis: The criterion asked for false alarms to be measured against English and technical text.
theTicketsHypothesisWasWrong.measured: Neither corpus produced a single English or technical false alarm at any threshold. The dominant false alarm is SHORT, entirely correct Swedish that happens to need no diacritic: 'PR #49 mergad som e94f730d och finns i live-builden', 'Janitorn ska trimma sessionsloggar per rad, inte radera hela filer', 'Varje har ett jobb.'
theTicketsHypothesisWasWrong.consequence: For a short paragraph the rule is unsound in principle rather than miscalibrated: there is too little text for the absence of a diacritic to carry information. The fix is a length floor, not a better word list.

lengthSweep.method: Flag counts over the same 6937 paragraphs at rising length floors, scored against the 17 exhaustively hand-audited false alarms found at the lowest floor.
lengthSweep.cost: Raising the floor from 8 to 40 gives up 63 flags. 17 of those were the false alarms; the other 46 were real but short mangling, deliberately conceded to reach a clean operating point.

audit.method: At the lowest floor every flagged paragraph that an automatic classifier could not confirm as mangled was read by hand. 100% of that residue was reviewed; nothing was sampled. The flag set at floor 40 is a strict SUBSET of the flag set at floor 8, and contains none of the 17 enumerated false alarms, so its zero follows from the same audit rather than from a second, weaker one.
audit.doNotCalibrateOn: The stripped-diacritic word list used to pre-sort the residue UNDERSTATES the damage: paragraphs it could not confirm were mostly undetected mangling, not false alarms. The hand review is the acceptance number, not that list's precision.
audit.secondDialectFound: Part of the corpus is mangled as aa/ae/oe transliteration ('vaagen', 'anvaendare', 'floede') rather than as stripped diacritics. The criterion catches it too, because that text also contains no a-ring/umlaut.

independentCorroboration.corpus: 534 agent-authored board documents, disjoint from both corpora above
independentCorroboration.result: 96 flags across 51 documents (9.6%) at the same 40-word floor; 14 of 14 hand-reviewed flags were genuine damage, zero false alarms. Under 20 words: 17 flags, all noise.
independentCorroboration.why_it_matters: Two independent measurements on disjoint corpora selected the same operating point.

decision.why: The ticket requires a measured number before a flaky gate is switched on. The number is now clean enough to justify blocking, but flipping a warning into a rejection changes what happens to an author's work and is a deliberate decision with an owner, not a side effect of a measurement.
decision.beforeBlocking: Re-run bin/measure-mangled-swedish.mjs, re-audit the residue by hand, and move the rejection ahead of stageSuggestionsRequest so a refused send leaves no envelope behind (#284).

incidentalFinding.what: 184 paragraphs of agent-authored Swedish in these two corpora alone had already lost every diacritic before this check existed, plus 96 more in ai:2's board corpus.
incidentalFinding.why: AI-0014 made DECLARED quotes byte-exact. Text mangled while it was being written was never declared, so nothing ever looked at it. This is the size of that gap, measured.
